## Scope

This gallery summarizes GnRHcell outputs stored in the five bundled Seurat demo
objects. The objects cover hPSC-derived GnRH differentiation, the developing
human nose, the human median eminence, and integrated mouse and human
hypothalamic references.

The objects are compact, preprocessed, and intentionally retain GnRH-relevant
cells. Consequently, detection fractions in this gallery are **not estimates of
GnRH-cell prevalence** in the source tissues or complete atlases.

## Detection across demo objects

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%", eval=TRUE}
knitr::include_graphics("../man/figures/demo-umap-status.png")
```

Red points are cells classified as `gnrh_status == "pos"`; grey points are all
other cells. GnRH-detected cells occupy localized or connected transcriptional
neighborhoods in each demo embedding. The figure is descriptive of the bundled
objects and does not establish sensitivity or specificity against an external
reference annotation.

## Numerical summary

| Demo dataset | Species | Cells | GnRH detected | Identity | Migrating | Mature | Secreting |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| hPSC-derived GnRH | Human | 2,400 | 657 | 341 | 118 | 198 | 0 |
| Human fetal nose | Human | 2,125 | 125 | 57 | 58 | 10 | 0 |
| Human median eminence | Human | 2,161 | 161 | 42 | 25 | 94 | 0 |
| Mouse HypoMap | Mouse | 2,174 | 174 | 10 | 0 | 164 | 0 |
| Human HypoMap | Human | 2,400 | 400 | 27 | 105 | 268 | 0 |

The machine-readable table is available as
[`demo-results.csv`](https://github.com/ymbouamboua/GnRHcell/blob/main/man/figures/demo-results.csv).
Values are derived directly from `gnrh_status` and `gnrh_stage` in the bundled
objects.

## Developmental-stage composition

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="95%", eval=TRUE}
knitr::include_graphics("../man/figures/demo-stage-composition.png")
```

The hPSC-derived and fetal-nose objects retain substantial identity and
migrating populations. The hypothalamic references are dominated by cells
classified as mature, consistent with their tissue context. These assignments
represent model-based hypotheses for downstream marker analysis and experimental
validation.

## Reproduce the summary

```{r reproduce-summary}
library(GnRHcell)

ids <- c(
  "hpsc", "hudeca_nose", "human_me",
  "mouse_hypomap", "human_hypomap"
)

objects <- setNames(
  lapply(ids, function(id) {
    readRDS(system.file("extdata", paste0(id, ".rds"), package = "GnRHcell"))
  }),
  ids
)

summarise_demo <- function(object) {
  md <- object[[]]
  positive <- md$gnrh_status == "pos"

  data.frame(
    cells = nrow(md),
    gnrh_detected = sum(positive, na.rm = TRUE),
    identity = sum(md$gnrh_stage == "identity", na.rm = TRUE),
    migrating = sum(md$gnrh_stage == "migrating", na.rm = TRUE),
    mature = sum(md$gnrh_stage == "mature", na.rm = TRUE),
    secreting = sum(md$gnrh_stage == "secreting", na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

do.call(rbind, lapply(objects, summarise_demo))
```

The static assets used by the README and this page can be regenerated from the
package root with:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/build-demo-gallery.R
```

## Interpretation checklist

- Treat the demo objects as examples of package behavior, not population-level
  sampling frames.
- Use an independent truth annotation for external ROC analysis.
- Confirm stage assignments with marker expression, donor consistency, and
  biological context.
- Cite both GnRHcell and the primary study associated with each source dataset.
